newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa called to open flat to $5 lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa called to open flat to $5 lower.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open unchanged to $5 lower Friday as the dollar's strength against Sterling is expected to weigh on dollar-denominated New York cocoa, dealers said.
"It's called flat to $5 lower based on currency," a trader said. Sterling headed lower Friday in the wake of Labour's landslide victory in the British election.
In London, LIFFE cocoa futures hovered at slightly higher levels in thin trade early Friday. At the midday break, July was up two stg at 990 stg a tonne, traded 995 to 988 stg.

Thursday, New York cocoa futures sagged to more than a two-month low, pressured by continued speculative liquidation. Benchmark July futures finished down $9 at $1,391 a tonne, near the bottom of its $1,390 to $1,404 range. Spot May slumped $14 to $1,380, while the rest ended $3 to $12 lower.

Technically, traders said cocoa's stance looked increasingly bearish after falling $85 in five days. To reverse the trend, July would need to settle above $1,400, traders said. Major resistance awaited at $1,418, followed by $1,450.
To the downside, the $1,385 area was viewed as nearby support, with the next area seen at $1,365 to $1,360. ((--Patricia Avidan, New York Commodity Desk 212 859 1640))
